title: M2 Issues: compose, render, approve for a time and send exactly once, with a web archive
description:
Outcome: an admin approves an issue for a time and the backend sends it, once per subscriber, with a web archive copy. First issue of The Docket.

Scope:
- Issue as a CMS item type with draft, review, approved-for-time (scheduled), sending, sent, cancelled. Composed by editors, optionally assembled from published items.
- Email renderer: Markus to email-safe HTML (tables, inlined CSS, dark mode, Outlook) plus a plain-text part; per-site template and sponsor slots through a plugin seam like the SiteProjector; rendered output stored in S3 and indexed in DynamoDB.
- Preview in the newsroom and test send to a few saved addresses (one per mail app the team checks).
- Admin-only approval creates a one-time EventBridge Scheduler schedule (UTC, shown in the publication time zone); its id is on the issue record. Cancel deletes it, reschedule updates it.
- At fire time a Step Functions send run re-validates status and the approved content hash (edited since approval: back to draft, nothing sent), then fans out through SQS at the SES per-second rate.
- Recipient-by-issue send ledger so a crashed or retried run never mails anyone twice; a stop flag checked between batches is the kill switch once sending has started; progress (sent, failed, suppressed) visible in the newsroom.
- Reply-To routes to the existing inbound email feature so reader replies land in Messages.
- Web archive: each sent issue is projected to the public site (for Distinctive Mark, /docket/<date>/) through the S3 projection.

Done when: an admin schedules a Docket issue for a future time and signs out; it sends at that time to every confirmed subscriber exactly once; an edit after approval prevents the send; cancel before and stop during a send both work; the issue appears in the web archive.
